- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes in true values; model tends to peak too early and then decay too slowly.
- Underestimate during periods of sustained high volatility or mean-reversion; model fails to capture downward momentum in volatile regimes.
- Exhibit lag in response to true price spikes; model often reacts 1–2 days too late, missing the peak or overshooting the trough.
- Overconfident in short-term trends; model frequently overestimates upward momentum in the first 5–7 days after a spike.
- Underestimate mean reversion in the final 5–7 days of the forecast; model holds onto high values longer than observed.
- Sensitive to recent history; model overweights recent low values when forecasting upward moves, leading to underestimation of true peaks.
- Tends to underestimate true values when the history includes a recent low followed by a sharp recovery — model fails to recognize the “rebound” phase.
- Overestimates in the final 3–5 days of the forecast when true values are trending downward — model fails to adjust for momentum reversal.
